title: Residency telemetry signal priorities and thresholds
body:
Purpose:
This is a working priorities doc for residency-related telemetry we want emitted, routed and acted upon during region pin enforcement, soft-failures, and migration windows. The goal is to reduce noisy alerts by scoring signals, assign owners, and prescribe thresholds and sample queries so SRE / Residency on-call can triage fast.

Background and constraints:
- We need high-fidelity evidence when a tenant is pinned to a region (hard pin) or soft-anchored to an edge.
- Telemetry must be economized: full traces for every request are expensive; prefer counters + sampled traces + deterministic evidence capture on exceptions.
- Signals should map to three operational outcomes: No action needed, Investigate (ticket + sampling), Emergency mitigation (failover / rollback / customer comms).

Priority signals (ranked):
1) Pin assertion failures (P1):
   - Why: direct indicator that a request violated the declared residency constraint (routing or storage mismatch).
   - Action: immediate page to residency-oncall + create ticket auto-populated with request ids.
   - Threshold: > 1 failure/min sustained for 3 consecutive minutes for a given tenant OR any single failure for enterprise tier customers.
   - Evidence needed: request id, tenant id, asserted_region, routed_region, KMS key location, timestamp, brief error message.
   - Example query (PromQL-ish): sum(rate(pin_assert_fail_total{tenant=~".*"}[1m])) by (tenant) > 1

2) Cross-region data writes detected (P1-high):
   - Why: writes committed to non-anchored region may be regulatory breach.
   - Action: immediate mitigation patch (quarantine writes) + legal/CS notification for high-tier customers.
   - Threshold: any committed write to a region outside tenant.allowed_regions within 10s of request acceptance.
   - Evidence: write_id, object_key, commit_region, tenant.policy_snapshot, deployment instance id.

3) Eviction / pin rollback events (P2):
   - Why: indicates operator actions that change residency; can trigger downstream routing/fallbacks and needs telemetry to prove customer guarantees.
   - Action: create a changelog entry and send to onboarding CS for affected customers; run reconciliation job.
   - Threshold: any programmatic rollback OR > 10% of tenant sessions affected in a 5-minute window.

4) Routing fidelity degradation (P2):
   - Metric: percent of requests routed to non-preferred-region for pinned tenants (rolling 5m).
   - Thresholds: 0.5% (info), 2% (investigate), 5% (page).
   - Query note: use routed_region != tenant.pin_region AND request_result=200 to isolate routing-only degradations.

5) KV cache misses for pinned-tenants (P3):
   - Why: cache misses cause cross-region fetches which may expose data movement.
   - Action: monitor trend and trigger cache warming experiment before rolling a fix.
   - Threshold: > 3x baseline miss-rate for tenant for 30 minutes.

6) Telemetry gaps / evidence-absence (P1/P2 depending):
   - Why: missing logs (no region tag, missing tenant id) is itself an incident risk for audits.
   - Action: page infra-logging oncall if > 1% of requests missing required residency metadata across a region for 10m.

Sampling and cost controls:
- Default sampling: 1% of successful requests for tenant-level traces; always-sample on pin-assert-failures and cross-region writes.
- For enterprise/high-risk tenants set sampling to 100% for 24h after any pin-related incident.
- Store full evidence bundle (request id, headers, routing decision, KMS tag) for pinned-tenants for 30 days; aggregated telemetry retained per normal SLO.

Alert routing and runbook mapping (quick):
- Pager to residency-oncall (primary) for P1 signals, and to sres-routing for P2 routing fidelity pages.
- Slack channel: #residency-ops for high-sev chat + quickcontext bot posts summary.
- Runbooks: attach /confluence/residency/runbooks/pin-assert-failure to alerts automatically.

Operator evidence capture template (what goes in ticket):
- Tenant ID, tier, contract pin date
- Last 10 request ids with timestamps and routed_region
- Snapshot of tenant.allowed_regions / policy id
- KMS key location and blob ids touched
- Operator actions since incident start (who, what, why)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who owns legal notifications for cross-region write breaches? (CS or Legal?) TODO: confirm with Legal — @Marta
- Standardize label names across proxies for routed_region vs destination_region. PR created (JIRA-OPS-2191).
- Implement sample ingestion pipeline to surface the 30-day evidence bundles into the audit UI. Owner: Ethan. ETA: Q3.

Appendix: quick prometheus-ish queries and example alert definitions
- pin_assert_fail_alert:
  expr: sum(rate(pin_assert_fail_total[1m])) by (tenant) > 1
  for: 3m
  labels: severity=critical, team=residency
  annotations: runbook_url=/confluence/residency/runbooks/pin-assert-failure

- routed_to_wrong_region_ratio:
  expr: sum(rate(requests_routed_wrong_region_total[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total[5m])) by (region, tenant)
  thresholds: 0.005, 0.02, 0.05

Notes on evidence retention policy tradeoffs:
- 30-day full-evidence retention increases storage but dramatically reduces audit friction. We propose a tiered bill-back for customers exceeding baseline. See finance model RFC (CONFLUENCE-6823).

Quick changelog:
- v0.1 2024-03-05 initial draft (Priya)
- v0.2 2024-05-21 added sampling rules and alert thresholds (Ethan)
- v0.3 2024-07-12 tightened P1 thresholds for enterprise tenants (Marta)

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally prescriptive in thresholds to prompt test runs in the staging observability cluster. Please leave inline comments or push PRs against JIRA-OPS-2191.
